paper_title: GPdoemd: A Python package for design of experiments for model discrimination
mechanistic_insights: The paper proposes a new design criterion for model discrimination using the Jensen-Rényi divergence, which explicitly maximizes the divergence of model predictive distributions.
A novel method is developed that replaces complex black-box models with Gaussian process (GP) surrogate models to facilitate the design of experiments.
The GP surrogate method allows for the application of classical analytical design of experiment techniques to non-analytical or black-box models for which gradients are not available.
Different design criteria (DBH, DBF, DAW, DJR) represent different trade-offs between the risk of partial discrimination and the reward of complete discrimination among models.
The paper introduces an open-source Python package, GPdoemd, which implements the GP surrogate method for designing experiments.

quantitative_outcomes.notes: This is a computational methods paper focused on the design of experiments for model discrimination. It does not report any synthetic chemistry, reaction conditions, or yields. The case studies (e.g., ammonia synthesis, chemical kinetics) are used to test the performance of the proposed computational algorithms, not to develop new chemical processes.
